name: Sahel insurgency
value: Insurgency sustained; no capital newly fallen
summary: JNIM and IS Sahel fight state forces and each other in Burkina Faso and Mali; no capital or major city has fallen
state: Al Qaeda-linked JNIM and Islamic State Sahel Province are fighting each other as well as state forces in Burkina Faso and Mali; IS claimed more than 400 JNIM fighters killed around Ganadaouri on 9 Oct, a figure not independently confirmed (Al Jazeera, 13 Nov). ACLED recorded more than 10,000 deaths from political violence in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger in January–November 2025. JNIM has expanded into Benin and Togo, but no new fall or blockade of a capital or major city and no new mass-casualty attack in a coastal state was found as of 17 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: The FCDO advises against all or most travel to large parts of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger; check its travel advice. The violence drives displacement across West Africa and raises pressure on coastal states such as Benin and Togo.
rubric_hit: Watch: sustained insurgency at current levels; no capital or major city fallen or newly blockaded

sources.title: Burkina Faso's rival armed groups turn on each other as state loses ground

why: Jihadist groups control growing territory across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, driving displacement and coastal-state spillover.
drivers: JNIM/IS-Sahel offensives, juntas, Russian forces, blockades, coastal-state attacks.

rubric.alert: Blockade or fall of a capital or major city, or mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states.
